data.narrative:
Compound Eye is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jason Devitt and Haoyang Wang that has raised $20.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public entity in the robotics and manufacturing sector, with three direct stage peers informing the primary benchmark set.

Two valuation methodologies were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised ($21M) as a base proxy and applying a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier for Series B advancement, yields $39M. Peer-median methodology applied the median valuation of three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—producing a $1.8B implied valuation with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis across these two methods produces a wide implied range: $33M (low), $895M (median), and $2.0B (high). The stage-progression method reflects Compound Eye's modest capital raised relative to later-stage rounds, while the peer-median approach anchors to market comparables. The substantial spread between methods reflects material uncertainty regarding whether this company should be valued as an early-stage capital-efficient operator or as a peer to well-funded robotics competitors. Resolution of this uncertainty depends on revenue traction, technical differentiation, and customer pipeline maturity relative to the stated comp set.
